answer: Each identity keeps a private pigment recipe: a blend of its own past verified contributions, committed publicly by hash. Each epoch it mixes a fresh pigment with the epoch seed and paints a sonnet, a structured original text on the epoch theme. Peers check the sonnet against the public recipe commitment and grade its originality; a copied recipe fails, since the hash binds it to one identity and the mix must differ each epoch. Only recipes that deepen over many epochs pass the velvet gate to paid work, so a sybil army must do real, distinct, sustained work for every identity it fields.
